title: Jeffrey Ketland
text:
These are the webpages of Jeffrey Ketland.

Email: jeffreyketland@gmail.com

I am retired Philosopher of Science. I retired in late 2025 as a Research Professor at the University of Warsaw. Prior to that, I have worked at the London School of Economics, and Kings College London, and the Universities of Nottingham, Cambridge, Leeds, Edinburgh, Munich and Oxford.

title: Research
text:
My research lies in Philosophy of Science, broadly construed. I am particularly interested in:

Formalization of scientific theories
Philosophy of applied mathematics
Truth, paradoxes and axiomatic systems of truth

Book

The Application of Mathematics: Entanglement and Instantiation. Cambridge University Press, 2026.
Description: Why is abstract mathematics applicable within science? Jeffrey Ketland describes the metatheory of the application of mathematics in science and highlights the ‘entanglement’ of physical systems with mathematical objects and structures. Applied Mathematics inferences are regimented into ‘canonical form’, involving an ambient foundational base theory and the specific physical premises and conclusions. These latter are formulated using concepts called ‘entanglers’, which relate physical objects and systems to mathematical objects. The simplest example is the membership predicate, ‘x is an element of y’, and other examples are coordinate functions, quantity functions (such as mass, length, or temporal duration), and fields (on space or spacetime). Mathematical terms denoting these, as well as impure sets, relations, and structures, are called ‘entanglement constants’. Ketland shows that such inferences satisfy a form of topic neutrality called Hilbert’s Beermug Principle, and all such inferences can be seen to be instantiations of general mathematical theorems with such constants.

Published articles
Refereed Articles

2023: Axiomatization of Galilean Spacetime. Dialectica, 77 (2): 153–202.
Description: Provides a second-order synthetic axiomatization \(\mathsf{Gal}(1,3)\)$\mathsf{Gal}(1,3)$ for Galilean spacetime—the background spacetime of Newtonian classical mechanics—using primitive notions of betweenness, simultaneity, and hypersurface congruence.
2022b: Standard Formalization. Global Philosophy, 32 (Suppl 3): 711–748.
Description: Explores simple and elegant methods for constructing standard first-order formalizations of mathematicized scientific theories involving differential equations and scalar fields.
2022a: Boolos’s Curious Inference in Isabelle/HOL. Archive of Formal Proofs (July 2022).
Description: Formalizes George Boolos’s demonstration of the computational and deductive speed-up of higher-order logic over first-order logic, verifying fourteen constituent lemmas using Isabelle/HOL.

Personal Details

Born: 20 March 1964, Birmingham, England.
Residence: Liberton, Edinburgh, Scotland.
Email: jeffreyketland@gmail.com
Twitter: @jeffreyketland

Education

1975 – 1982: King Edwards Camp Hill School for Boys, Birmingham.
1982 – 1985: Trinity College, Cambridge. BA Theoretical Physics.
1985 – 1986: Trinity College, Cambridge. Part III Maths Tripos.
1990 – 1992: University of Warwick. MA Philosophy.
1994 – 1998: London School of Economics & Political Science. PhD Philosophy of Science.

Work

1991 – 1991: Teaching Assistant, University of Warwick.
1996 – 1998: Temporary Lecturer, Richmond College.
1996 – 1998: Teaching Assistant, LSE.
1998 – 1999: Temporary Lecturer, LSE.
2000 – 2001: Lecturer, University of Nottingham.
2001 – 2002: Post-doctoral Fellow, King’s College London.
2002 – 2003: Temporary Lecturer, University of Leeds.
2003 – 2004: Temporary Lecturer, University of Cambridge.
2004 – 2011: Lecturer, University of Edinburgh.
2011 – 2012: Lecturer, University of Munich.
2012 – 2016: Associate Professor & Fellow, University of Oxford, Pembroke College.
2019 – 2025: Research Professor, University of Warsaw.
2025 – present: Retired.
